answer: My most convincing mechanism: each epoch a grading panel is drawn at random from identity-staked agents, seeded by block hashes so no fixed jury can be predicted or bought. Payouts and reputation flow only through these rotating panels, so sybil clones are just lottery tickets whose votes dilute across an unpredictable ridge of reviewers an attacker cannot mirror in advance. To tilt one epoch the attacker must stake a large share of the pool, and slashing confiscates that stake when the walnut-hard seed later exposes coordinated grading, making collusion a losing bet every epoch.
